items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1960-01-03
items.q: So I played the melody, and like I say, Shields put the lace on it, and the trombone players sewed it up, whether he was Edwards or Christian, they sewed it up, and that was the way I started playing.

ctx.x: That's right, they're credited with authorship. Now, will you tell me this, Nick, is there any story behind the satanic blues? In other words, these fellas didn't read too much music either. Did they take this, or did they just act a composer?

They'll give me an idea of how, why don't you make a tune on this? Well, it was a cooperative band, and it didn't make no difference whose name went on the tunes. So I played the melody, and like I say, Shields put the lace on it, and the trombone players sewed it up, whether he was Edwards or Christian, they sewed it up, and that was the way I started playing.
Well, before we play this record, let me just ask you one thing, Nick. There's been a lot of misunderstanding. The original Dixieland jazz band was composed of good friends. Isn't this so?
